title: NIST: standard atomic weight of Nitrogen (N, Z=7) is the interval [14.00643,14.00728]
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Nitrogen (N, Z=7) as [14.00643,14.00728], with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 7, symbol N, as Nitrogen. The NIST compositions file prints the standard atomic weight of Nitrogen as the interval [14.00643,14.00728]. This interval is the set of atomic-weight values NIST assigns to normal materials. It is not the uncertainty of one weighing. The notes field on this element's rows is blank. Isotope rows in the same file: N-14 relative atomic mass 14.00307400443(20), isotopic composition 0.99636(20); N-15 relative atomic mass 15.00010889888(64), isotopic composition 0.00364(20). A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
